 Suspect arrested in investigation into explosive device found at Illinois ethanol plant, official says
 By Evan Perez , Andy Rose 
 Updated Nov 16, 2026, 10:08 AM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 16, 2026, 8:45 AM ET 
 Peoria Police Department officers on scene at a reported bomb threat at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria, Illinois, on November 13, 2026. 
 WEEK-TV

 A suspect has been arrested in connection with an investigation into an explosive device found Friday at a central Illinois ethanol plant, according to a law enforcement official.
 The suspect was arrested Monday, morning and the investigation continues into others who may have been involved, the official said.
 The discovery of the device at BioUrja Renewables forced thousands of people to evacuate Peoria’s downtown area for a day as investigators searched the sprawling industrial facility to rule out any further threats.
 Because of the materials inside the facility, the device could have resulted in a one-mile blast radius if it had gone off, Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said Friday .
 The FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives are involved in the investigation, the official told CNN, who said it was not yet clear if the device was viable. There is no suspected nexus to foreign terrorism at this point, according to the official.
 The city of Peoria, located along the Illinois River 130 miles southwest of Chicago, has a population of more than 100,000. The BioUrja plant is near Peoria’s downtown and was built in the 1930s, Mayor Rita Ali said.
 “We’ve had a real life Friday the 13th nightmare,” Ali told CNN’s Jessica Dean over the weekend.
 CNN reached out to the Peoria Police Department Monday for further information about the arrest and what charges may be filed.
 The evacuation lasted about 24 hours. The device did not explode, and no one was hurt during the incident.
 “Thank you to our tireless law enforcement officers and first responders on call who worked around the clock to keep Peoria safe,” Gov. JB Pritzker wrote on Facebook .
 The evacuation order caused some downtown events to be cancelled or rescheduled, including a minor league hockey game and a portion of Illinois Comic Con .
 This is a developing story and will be updated. 
 CNN’s Laura Sharman, Martin Goillandeau and Eduardo Cuevas contributed to this report.
